records.summary: Creates a behind-the-meter self-power system category that lets large non-residential customers be served by on-site or adjacent generation and storage without using utility wires, including third-party-owned systems. It also taxes new energy storage as generation property at a lower assessment rate and sets fixed Ohio Power Siting Board review deadlines, with a faster track for certified brownfield and former coal-mine sites.
records.note: Dates are from the legislature's status page. Provision details are from a law-firm summary, not the statute text. Self-power systems are allowed in rural cooperative territory only for new load centers.

records.title: House Bill 646 (136th General Assembly) - Create the Data Center Study Commission
records.summary: Would create a state commission to study data centers. It passed the House on 2026-03-18, was reported by the Senate Energy Committee on 2026-06-10 and was sent back to that committee the same day without a final Senate vote.
records.note: House passage is not enactment. Content of Senate amendments was not reviewed; status as shown on the legislature's page when opened on 2026-11-09.

records.title: House Bill 96 (FY2026-27 operating budget) provision ending the data-center sales-tax exemption - vetoed
records.summary: The legislature's 2025 budget removed the sales-tax exemption for data-center construction materials, and Governor DeWine vetoed that provision, so the exemption survived. In June 2026 the House Speaker said he lacked the votes to override.
records.note: News only. statusDate is the report date; the exact veto date was not stated in the opened articles. A 2026 package to shrink new tax breaks was pulled from a joint committee vote in June 2026.

records.title: Senate Bill 106 (136th General Assembly) - Regulate the ownership of electric vehicle charging stations
records.summary: Classifies EV charging stations as a competitive retail electric service that consumers may obtain from any supplier. Under the Senate-passed version, this means PUCO-regulated electric utilities cannot provide charging stations, and charging providers remain subject to PUCO certification.
records.note: The substance is taken from the LSC analysis of the As Passed by the Senate version. The House amended the bill before the Senate concurred (2026-06-03), and the enrolled text was not reviewed, so check the final act for exceptions.

records.jurisdiction: State of Ohio (Governor / Ohio Tax Credit Authority)
records.title: Governor's pause on new data-center sales-tax exemption requests
records.summary: At the Governor's direction, the Ohio Tax Credit Authority stopped accepting new data-center exemption proposals after its next scheduled meeting. The pause lasts while the legislature's Joint Data Center Committee studies the industry, and the release describes it as a pause on requests rather than a ban on data centers.
records.note: No end date is given. The release does not address exemptions already granted. Whether the pause has since been lifted was not verified.

sources.publisher: Office of the Governor of Ohio

records.jurisdiction: State of Ohio (Public Utilities Commission of Ohio)
records.title: PUCO Case 24-508-EL-ATA: AEP Ohio data-center-specific tariff
records.summary: The commission adopted a settlement among AEP Ohio, PUCO staff, the Ohio Consumers' Counsel and others, and ordered AEP Ohio to file new tariffs that apply specifically to data centers. The same order told the utility to lift its pause on connecting new data centers as soon as possible.
records.note: The opened bulletin does not state the tariff's MW threshold, minimum-demand percentage or contract term; read the order in the docket for those. Applies in AEP Ohio territory only. Rehearing or appeal outcome not checked.

records.jurisdiction: State of Ohio (Public Utilities Commission of Ohio)
records.title: PUCO Case 26-113-EL-ATA: AEP Ohio default-service protections from data-center load
records.summary: A finding and order requires data-center customers to give AEP Ohio 180 days' notice before returning to the utility's default supply. AEP Ohio must then buy their energy through separate auctions or spot purchases, with the full cost assigned to that customer rather than to other default-service customers.
records.note: AEP Ohio territory only. Tariff effective date not stated in the bulletin.

records.jurisdiction: State of Ohio (Public Utilities Commission of Ohio)
records.title: PUCO directive to FirstEnergy's Ohio utilities on data-center transmission charges
records.summary: Regulators reportedly gave FirstEnergy's three Ohio utilities 30 days to propose higher transmission charges for large data centers as their load grows. This extends the data-center pricing approach beyond AEP Ohio.
records.note: Source is a trade association post that opposes such tariffs, not the PUCO order. Case number and order date are not given; statusDate is the post date. Whether FirstEnergy filed, and any commission ruling, not verified.

records.title: Proposed constitutional amendment: Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center (over 25 MW)
records.summary: A citizen petition would bar data centers above 25 megawatts statewide. The Ballot Board cleared it as a single amendment in spring 2026, but the campaign fell far short of the roughly 413,000 signatures needed by July 1 and will not be on the November 2026 ballot; organizers say they are now aiming for 2027.
records.note: News only. Not law and not yet on any ballot; 76,626 signatures were reported as of late June 2026. Status of the 2027 drive not verified.

records.title: Ordinance 70-26: one-year temporary moratorium on data centers
records.summary: Council unanimously adopted a one-year moratorium on data centers, covering both AI and large-scale data-storage facilities, while the city studies impacts and writes regulations. The mayor or service-safety director may extend it by one more year.
records.note: News only. Applies inside city limits; Athens Township reportedly adopted a separate data-center resolution in August 2026 (not opened).

records.title: EV Ready Parking Ordinance (zoning code amendment)
records.summary: A zoning code amendment requires newly constructed parking lots to include EV charging provision for tenants, residents and visitors. Council approved it in July 2022 and it took effect at the start of 2024.
records.note: Adopted before the 2023 window but effective inside it. The opened page gives no percentages by use type and no ordinance number in text (a link suggests 1617-2022); read the ordinance for the actual ratios. City limits only.

records.title: 18-month moratorium on data center construction and new outside water requests
records.summary: Council approved an 18-month moratorium on data-center construction inside the city and on new requests for city water to serve developments in outside jurisdictions. It can end early if council adopts standards first.
records.note: News only. statusDate is the report date; the vote was the Monday before (six in favor, one abstention). Does not affect the existing water agreement for the Google data center in American Township. A separate Shawnee Township (Allen County) moratorium covering data centers, battery storage and solar was reported but its source could not be opened, so it is not recorded here.

sources.publisher: The Lima News via Government Technology

records.title: One-year moratorium on new data center developments
records.summary: Trustees voted unanimously for a one-year pause on new data-center development while the township studies power and water capacity and rewrites its zoning rules.
records.note: Applies only to unincorporated parts of the township; land annexed into Grove City is outside it. Source is the trustees' community letter, not the resolution, so no resolution number or exact end date.

records.title: Nine-month moratorium on new data centers
records.summary: Trustees unanimously paused new data-center construction for nine months after complaints about noise from two existing Amazon facilities. The stated aim was to revise zoning so that data centers become a conditional rather than a permitted use.
records.note: News only. A nine-month term from September 2025 would have run out around June 2026; no source confirming an extension or the resulting zoning amendment was found. Do not confuse with Jerome Township, Michigan, which has similar 2026 records online. Expiry date computed from the stated term and start date, not stated by the source.

records.title: Resolution establishing a temporary (two-year) moratorium on construction of data centers over 25 MW
records.summary: Trustees voted unanimously for a resolution that starts the township zoning-amendment process to prohibit construction of data centers with demand above 25 megawatts for two years. The text is referred to the township zoning commission and county planning commission for hearing before it returns to the trustees.
records.note: News describes this as an adopted moratorium, but the resolution text initiates a zoning amendment under R.C. 519.12, so final adoption and the effective date were not verified. The resolution copy is unsigned and hosted by a news outlet.

sources.publisher: Montgomery Township resolution text, hosted by Ashland Source

records.title: Resolution 2026-002 initiating a zoning moratorium for data center uses (extended)
records.summary: An eight-month moratorium adopted 2026-02-11 bars the township from accepting, processing or issuing zoning permits, certificates or site-plan approvals for data centers while zoning text is drafted. Trustees later extended it to 2027-05-31 and said no data center is under consideration at any site in the township.
records.note: The extension is from news only; statusDate is the report date (the vote was described as Tuesday night). The posted resolution copy is unsigned.

records.title: Resolution 26-056 placing a moratorium on data centers
records.summary: Trustees voted 3-0 for a six-month moratorium on locating or operating any new data center in the township. They also resolved to consider adding a data-center section to the zoning code during the pause.
records.note: Six months from 2026-04-14 would have run out around mid-October 2026; no extension or follow-on zoning amendment was verified. Township only, not the City of Ravenna. Expiry date computed from the stated term and start date, not stated by the source.

records.title: Six-month moratorium on zoning permits for data centers and solar fields
records.summary: Trustees approved a six-month moratorium on zoning permits for data centers and solar fields, running from 2026-05-05 to 2026-11-05. A longer one-year term was discussed but not adopted.
records.note: News only. The stated expiry date has passed; whether it was extended is not verified. The county is not named in the article (Fulton is from general knowledge). Battery storage is not mentioned.

records.title: 180-day moratorium on data center permits (extended), upheld by the Ohio Supreme Court
records.summary: Council first banned data centers in late 2025, replaced the ban with a 180-day moratorium in January 2026, and on 2026-07-06 extended it another 180 days, to January 2027. The Ohio Supreme Court unanimously held that, under the moratorium, the village has no duty to proceed with site-plan review for the proposed Bristolville 25 data center.
records.note: News only. The court opinion was not opened, and the ruling date is not stated in the opened article (reported as a Tuesday in October 2026). Exact expiry day in January 2027 not stated. Sets precedent that pre-filed preliminary plans do not vest against a later moratorium.

records.title: Six-month moratorium on data centers
records.summary: Trustees voted 3-0 for a six-month pause on building, zoning or approving data centers. The zoning commission is to review the issue and draft restrictions.
records.note: News only. statusDate is the report date; the vote was earlier that week. The article does not name the county (Trumbull is from general knowledge). The six-month term would have lapsed around early November 2026 unless extended; not verified.

records.title: HB 1600 (2024) - sales tax exemption for commercial digital asset mining equipment
records.summary: Creates a sales tax exemption through the end of 2029 for machinery, equipment and electricity used in commercial digital asset mining. The mining must take place in a qualified colocation facility that has a load reduction agreement with its retail electric supplier.
records.note: Provisions are from the conference committee substitute summary dated 5/28/2024, not the enrolled text. Bill page lists Governor approval 06/14/2024; other trackers show 05/30/2024.

records.title: HB 2156 (2025-26) - setbacks for utility-scale solar and industrial battery storage
records.summary: Would have set setback requirements for utility-scale solar and industrial battery storage facilities. It passed the House 73-23 in March 2025 and got a do-pass from Senate Energy, but the bill page shows no Senate floor vote.
records.note: The bill page does not label it dead. 'Expired' is my inference: no action after April 2025 and the 2025-26 Legislature has adjourned. Setback distances differed by version and were not verified.

records.title: HB 2992 - Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026
records.summary: Requires electric suppliers to put large-load customers (75 MW or more, including data centers, AI facilities and crypto mining) on separate tariffs and terms so other ratepayers do not carry their costs. Developers must notify adjoining landowners, county commissioners and the Corporation Commission within 60 days of acquiring land.
records.note: Bill page shows Governor approval 05/11/2026; the July 1, 2026 effective date comes from the House release and KGOU. Enrolled text was not read.

records.title: HB 3594 (2024) - digital asset mining protections
records.summary: Requires state and local governments to treat commercial digital asset mining the same as data centers and bars discriminatory utility rates for mining businesses. Home mining is allowed but stays subject to local noise ordinances.
records.note: Approval date is from the bill page; the provisions and effective date are from news coverage, not the enrolled text. Limits how far a locality can single out crypto mining.

records.title: HB 3724 (2026) - restrictions on high-demand electric facilities
records.summary: Would have banned taxpayer subsidies and cost shifting for high-demand facilities, barred them from agricultural land and foreign ownership, and let citizens petition against local siting decisions. It failed in the House Utilities Committee on a 2-6 vote.
records.note: News source only. statusDate is the article date; the article says the bill died that week.

records.title: SB 1488 (2026) - statewide moratorium on data centers of 100 MW or more
records.summary: Would have halted construction of data centers of 100 MW or more until November 1, 2029 and directed the Corporation Commission to study their impacts. It was referred to Senate Rules and Appropriations and never received a hearing or vote.
records.note: Status 'expired' means it died in committee without a vote. statusDate is the last recorded action (a coauthor entry). Its sponsor said in October 2026 that a moratorium is still wanted for 2027.

records.title: SB 237 (2026) - ending the five-year manufacturer ad valorem exemption for solar and BESS
records.summary: Would have barred solar generation and battery energy storage systems from the five-year manufacturer ad valorem tax exemption starting January 2028. The Legislature passed it, but the Governor did not sign before the May 29, 2026 deadline, so it was pocket vetoed.
records.note: The existing exemption therefore still covers BESS. The House author's statement is the source.

records.title: SB 480 (2025) - behind-the-meter generation for large users
records.summary: Changes an exception in the utility definition so private industry can develop and manage its own on-site power and certain entities can receive that electricity. It was promoted as a way around grid-connection bottlenecks for large industrial loads.
records.note: Approval date is from the bill page. Eligibility details (load size, fuel requirements) and the effective date were not verified from the enrolled text.

records.title: SB 502 (2023) - Oklahoma Electric Vehicle Charging Act
records.summary: Lets private businesses operate EV chargers without competing against ratepayer-funded utility stations. A retail electric supplier may offer DC fast charging only through a separate unregulated entity on the same terms as private providers, and may not recover charger costs from other customers.
records.note: Codified at 17 O.S. 160.31-160.37 per AFDC. Effective date not shown on the pages opened.

sources.publisher: U.S. DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center

records.title: Senate interim studies on data centers (possible 2027 moratorium or guardrail legislation)
records.summary: Two Senate interim studies on October 28, 2026 covered data center environmental impacts and national security and tax questions. Sen. Sacchieri voiced support for a moratorium of about a year, and Sen. Murdock suggested statutory guardrails.
records.note: No bill filed yet. The next session begins February 1, 2027.

records.title: OG&E proposed large-load tariff (75 MW and above)
records.summary: OG&E filed a tariff on June 17, 2026 that would put customers of 75 MW or more in a separate class. They would pay for estimated usage whether used or not, fund their own grid connections and pay a monthly fee into a fund that could credit other customers.
records.note: Docket number not given in the sources. Tulsa Flyer reports the Commission will take the tariff up on Jan. 12 (2027 implied).

records.title: PSO large-load tariff approved in rate case (Case PUD 2025-000075)
records.summary: The Commission's November 5, 2026 order in PSO's rate case approved a new rate class with separate terms for customers adding more than 75 MW. It left open further study of how large loads may bring their own generation.
records.note: News only; the order was not read. Case number is from Oklahoma Energy Today. Tariff described as requiring long-term contracts and upfront financial guarantees. Treat terms as interim until the follow-on proceeding ends.

records.title: Six-month moratorium on data center land use applications
records.summary: The council unanimously stopped accepting land use applications for data centers because the zoning code has no data center rules. Local reports give a December 31 end date, with an option to extend six more months.
records.note: News only; the city's own page returned 403. Six months from June 15 is mid-December, yet both local outlets report December 31.

records.title: Ordinance No. 4091 - moratorium on data center rezoning and building permit applications
records.summary: Bars acceptance or processing of rezoning and building permit applications for data centers until December 31, 2026 or until data center regulations take effect. It covers AI computing facilities adding 75 MW or more and lets the council grant exemptions on appeal.
records.note: Passed 5-0 with emergency clause. The definition excludes entities that build behind-the-meter generation and ordinary residential, commercial, agricultural or industrial ratepayers.

records.title: Zoning amendment sorting data centers and digital asset mining by peak electrical demand
records.summary: The council voted 5-3 to allow data centers with peak demand of 2 MW or less by right in the I-1 district. Data centers or digital asset mining above 2 MW become a use permitted on review in the I-4 heavy industrial district.
records.note: News only; ordinance number not given. City limits only.

records.title: Ordinance O-2526-70 - temporary moratorium on data center rezonings, approvals and permits
records.summary: The council unanimously suspended acceptance and processing of rezoning requests and permits for new or expanded data centers through June 9, 2027 while the zoning code is updated. Appeals and hardship variances go to the Board of Adjustment.
records.note: Ordinance number and terms are from the staff report for first reading on June 9, 2026; the adopted text was not read. Applies only to applications filed after the effective date.

records.title: Temporary moratorium on new data center applications, rezonings and permits
records.summary: The council unanimously paused new data center applications, rezonings and permits until December 31, 2026 or until data center zoning amendments are adopted. A May 19, 2026 amendment (7-2) exempted two named projects and let facilities under 75 MW proceed.
records.note: City limits only. In late October 2026 the mayor said a six-month extension would be brought forward; I found no adoption vote, so check before relying on the December 31 end date.

records.title: Moratorium on data center considerations through 2026
records.summary: At a public works authority meeting, city officials voted 3-2 to halt any data center considerations through December 31, 2026. They also unanimously refused a load guarantee letter for a developer.
records.note: News only. The vote was reported at a public works authority meeting, so confirm whether the city council adopted a formal ordinance.

records.title: Rezoning of 827 acres for the Project Spring data center along Highway 97
records.summary: The council voted 6-1 to rezone 827 annexed acres along Highway 97 for a White Rose Partners data center to be operated by Google, despite heavy local opposition.
records.note: News only. A lawsuit over the annexation was pending at the time. Counties are those the city sits in; the site's county was not stated.

records.title: Temporary moratorium on new data center proposals
records.summary: City commissioners put new data center proposals on hold, effective immediately, through the end of 2027 while the city studies how to regulate them and updates its code.
records.note: News only. statusDate is the article date; the vote date and tally were not stated (a meeting listing suggests August 17, 2026).

records.title: Moratorium on new data center permits pending zoning code review
records.summary: The council unanimously paused processing and approval of new data center building permits through December 31, 2026 or until zoning rules are updated. Project Anthem phases one and two are exempt.
records.note: City limits only. A draft planning report floated size tiers and raising setbacks from protected uses from 250 ft to 1,500 ft (proposal, not adopted). Final recommendations were due November 2026; no outcome found.

records.title: Six-month moratorium on new data center applications
records.summary: The Board of Trustees voted for a six-month pause on new data center applications and took no action on the pending proposal. The same agenda carried a draft ordinance setting minimum requirements for data center applications.
records.note: News only. Date inferred: KFOR says the vote was on a Wednesday and the Luther Register says the meeting was rescheduled to Wednesday, June 17, 2026. Six months from then is about mid-December 2026.
